source_span.text_excerpt: Proposition 4. Homeomorphic spaces have isomorphic fundamental groups. If $f:X\rightarrow Y$ is a homeomorphism, then $f_ :\pi_1(X,x)\rightarrow \pi_1(Y,f(x))$ is an isomorphism.*

entries.statement: Proposition 4. Homeomorphic spaces have isomorphic fundamental groups. If $f:X\rightarrow Y$ is a homeomorphism, then $f_ :\pi_1(X,x)\rightarrow \pi_1(Y,f(x))$ is an isomorphism.*

source_span.text_excerpt: Corollary 5. Two homotopic equivalent spaces have the same fundamental group. If $f:X\rightarrow Y$ is a homotopy equivalence, then $f_ :\pi_1(X,x)\rightarrow \pi_1(Y,f(x))$ is an isomorphism.*

entries.statement: Corollary 5. Two homotopic equivalent spaces have the same fundamental group. If $f:X\rightarrow Y$ is a homotopy equivalence, then $f_ :\pi_1(X,x)\rightarrow \pi_1(Y,f(x))$ is an isomorphism.*

source_span.text_excerpt: Proposition 6. If $X$ is a path-connected topological space, then $\pi_1(X, x_0)$ and $\pi_1(X, x_1)$ are isomorphic for any $x_0,x_1\in X$.

entries.statement: Proposition 6. If $X$ is a path-connected topological space, then $\pi_1(X, x_0)$ and $\pi_1(X, x_1)$ are isomorphic for any $x_0,x_1\in X$.

source_span.text_excerpt: Proposition 10. Let $q:Z \rightarrow X$ be a connected cover and $f:Y \rightarrow Z$ be a continuous map. If the composition $q\circ f:Y \rightarrow X$ is a cover, then so is $f:Y \rightarrow X$.
